# libarchive / libarchive_write_fuzzer

libarchive's own fuzz target `libarchive_write_fuzzer` ([source](source/libarchive_write_fuzzer.cc), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over libarchive (libarchive/libarchive at 3670ecf7).

Writes up to 10 fuzz entries (file/dir/symlink, ids, mtime, <= 1 KiB data) in one of 8 formats (pax_restricted, gnutar, ustar, cpio newc, zip, 7zip, xar, pax) through one of gzip/bzip2/xz/zstd/none into a vector it never reads. It returns early if archive_write_new returns NULL or archive_write_open does not return ARCHIVE_OK, stops adding entries if archive_entry_new returns NULL, writes a file's data only when archive_write_header returns ARCHIVE_OK and the data is non-empty, and drops every other libarchive result. write_callback returns -1 if appending to the vector throws std::bad_alloc.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against libarchive at commit 3670ecf7.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source is modified: source/libarchive_write_fuzzer.cc is libarchive 3670ecf7's contrib/oss-fuzz/libarchive_write_fuzzer.cc with one Theorem Labs change. It catches std::bad_alloc from the harness's own allocation inside write_callback, which then returns -1, so libarchive's write fails and no exception passes through libarchive's C code.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing. Its halts statements say only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer. Its agreement statements say only that the code never crashes or trips a sanitizer, and allow a run that never ends.
